q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a backpack or school bag?
title: Backpack carbon footprint per piece
short: Weigh each material in the bag: polyester or nylon fabric, foam, webbing, zips and buckles. Multiply each by its supplier's per-kg figure, add cutting, stitching and packing energy, then divide the unit's electricity by bags passed.

ul: Coated polyester or nylon fabric by weight, including cutting waste.
Foam padding, mesh, webbing and binding tape.
Zips, sliders, buckles and plastic stiffeners.
Cutting presses, sewing and bar-tack machines.
Printing or heat transfer of logos.
Poly bags, hang tags and cartons.

p: Report per bag by model; the material list usually explains most of the difference between models.

example.title: Worked example: bag unit per piece (one month)
lines: Plant total: 12,780 / 30,000 = 0.426 kg CO2 per bag
Add fabric, foam, zips and buckles for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
